title: OrthographicCamera
cards/0/body:
An OrthographicCamera has no perspective: objects of the same size look the same up close and far away. The view pyramid becomes a box.

It is used for technical drawings and CAD views, isometric games, and 2D interfaces on top of 3D.
cards/1/q: Two identical cubes: one 2 meters away, the other 20. How do they look through an OrthographicCamera?
cards/1/options/1: The far one is 10 times smaller
cards/1/explain: Perspective shrinking only happens with a PerspectiveCamera.
cards/2/body: left, right, top, bottom are the box edges in scene units, and near, far work as before. To zoom, use the zoom property (and call updateProjectionMatrix() again after changing it).
cards/3/q: Where does an OrthographicCamera make sense? Select all that apply.
cards/3/options/0: A part drawing with exact dimensions
cards/4/q: The window got wider and the picture stretched. Which line in resize needs fixing?
cards/4/explain: The edges must depend on the aspect ratio: camera.left = -w / 2; camera.right = w / 2.
cards/5/pairs/0/1: Like an eye: far things look smaller
cards/5/pairs/1/1: Like a blueprint: sizes stay the same
cards/6/q: What do both cameras have in common?
cards/6/options/0: near, far, and the need to call updateProjectionMatrix after changes
cards/6/explain: Only the perspective camera has fov.
cards/7/explain: An ortho camera has no fov, so you zoom with zoom.
